story_title: A Careful Conversation at the Dental Clinic
paragraphs: Before her appointment, Noor had already {{mask_1}} the clinic that one of her molars had been sensitive for several weeks. At reception, she {{mask_2}}, "I also brought the notes from my previous dentist." The receptionist {{mask_3}} her that Dr. Patel was reviewing them. Noor {{mask_4}} that she was worried the tooth might need major treatment. She had been {{mask_5}} that a root canal was inevitable, but she wanted another opinion.

When Dr. Patel invited her in, Noor began by explaining what had happened. She wanted to {{mask_6}} the dentist exactly when the discomfort started. Dr. Patel {{mask_7}} her that the notes mentioned a large filling. He {{mask_8}}, "That does not automatically mean the tooth needs a root canal." Noor later {{mask_9}} that the explanation made her feel less anxious. She asked him to {{mask_10}} her whether the X-ray showed any damage near the nerve.

After examining the X-ray, Dr. Patel explained the possible causes of the sensitivity. He {{mask_11}} Noor that the nerve appeared healthy, although the filling might need adjustment. He also {{mask_12}} her to avoid chewing hard food on that side until the next visit. Then he {{mask_13}}, "We can monitor the tooth before deciding on further treatment." Noor {{mask_14}} to him, "I would prefer to understand each option before agreeing to a procedure."

Dr. Patel used a diagram to {{mask_15}} the difference between temporary sensitivity and signs of infection. He {{mask_16}} her that she should contact the clinic if the pain became constant or if swelling developed. Before leaving, Noor was {{mask_17}} to book a follow-up appointment in two weeks. The receptionist confirmed the time without {{mask_18}} her that the appointment could be changed if necessary.
At the desk, Noor {{mask_19}}, "Thank you for explaining the choices instead of rushing me." Dr. Patel {{mask_20}} her to call the clinic if she had any new symptoms before the follow-up.
